correctness.rationale: Compose two Jordan orbits with global C1 bi-Lipschitz F fixing 0. F has one constant orientation sign s; the image angular lifts wind by 2πsν_i. The push-forward residual angular component is bounded by Mε/|F(x)|≤Mε/(mr_i), pointwise on orbit i. Integrating for its primitive period gives |sω_i−Ω|≤Mε/(mr_i). The weighted two-orbit triangle inequality eliminates the single Ω and yields ε≥(m/M)(r1r2/(r1+r2))|ω1−ω2|. No monotonic polar angular speed assumption is used. The polynomial center f=(1+|x|²)Jx on radii 1,2 with Ω=4, F=identity gives both residual maxima exactly 2, equal to RHS2, proving universal-coefficient optimality in isometric case. Checked original exact rational verification source and independently reconstructed constants; finite arithmetic not used to prove all diffeomorphisms.

value.rationale: A structurally motivated model mismatch is quantified: if a nonlinear planar center has two unequal signed orbit frequencies, no global fixed-origin diffeomorphism with controlled condition numbers can transform one constant rotation into an exact simultaneous vector-field match. The bound depends on measurable radii and physical periods, and a polynomial equality case demonstrates sharpness in the natural isometric subclass. It is elementary but a precise positive model-class obstruction, more than a qualitative period mismatch or verification-only normalization check.
